content: Sphinx py domain gotcha: `None` in type annotations must be cross-referenced with the `obj` role, not `class` — Python's intersphinx inventory records None as py:data, so a py:class xref silently fails to resolve. Signature mode and description mode link annotations via SEPARATE code paths in sphinx/domains/python.py: `_parse_annotation`'s inner `make_xref` (signature mode) and `PyField`/`PyTypedField.make_xref` (description/docfield mode). A fix to None-linking must special-case `text == 'None' -> reftype 'obj'` in both. Also, `_parse_annotation`'s AST `unparse` needs explicit ast.Constant (py3.8+) / ast.NameConstant (py<3.8) handling, else any annotation containing None/True/... falls back to one un-linkable xref for the whole string.

content: sphinx/domains/python.py gotcha (3.0.x-era): _parse_annotation's inner unparse() builds node lists and strips the trailing ', ' separator with result.pop(). Empty elts break this in two ways: ast.Tuple (from `Tuple[()]`) pops an empty list -> IndexError; ast.List (from `Callable[[], X]`) silently pops the opening '[' punctuation instead. Fix: guard pops with `if node.elts:` and render empty tuple as '(' ')'. Quick verify without an app: call _parse_annotation directly and join astext(); full tests: PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sphinx_type_hint_links/stubs python -m pytest tests/test_domain_py.py -q.

content: Python ast gotcha (hit in Sphinx 3.0.x sphinx/util/inspect.py signature_from_str, bug #7773 "default value for positional-only argument vanished"): ast.arguments has ONE shared `defaults` list covering posonlyargs + args combined, right-aligned to the end of that combined sequence — it is NOT per-list. Any code iterating posonlyargs and args separately must offset into defaults (pad defaults on the left to len(posonlyargs)+len(args), then posonly arg i -> defaults[i], regular arg i -> defaults[i + len(posonlyargs)]). Sphinx's original code ignored defaults for posonlyargs entirely and indexed defaults relative to args.args only. kwonlyargs are fine: they have their own kw_defaults list. sphinx/pycode/ast.py handles this correctly and is a good reference implementation. Unit tests: tests/test_util_inspect.py -k signature_from_str (no app fixture needed, no env stubs required).

content: Sphinx autodoc mock gotcha (sphinx/ext/autodoc/mock.py, hit in 3.1.x bug #7853): _MockObject.__getitem__ receives non-str keys — subscripting a mocked class as a generic base (`class Foo(MockedBase[T])`) passes a TypeVar — but _make_subclass requires a str name (it does `module + '.' + name` and `type(name, ...)`), so it raised TypeError. Fix (matches upstream 3.1.2): type __getitem__ key as Any and call _make_subclass(str(key), ...); __getattr__ keys are always str so it needs no change. Verified by tests/test_ext_autodoc_mock.py (no app fixture needed — runs without the sphinxcontrib stubs).

Sphinx napoleon gotcha (sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py _skip_member, bug #4335 "decorated __init__ not documented"): to decide cls_is_owner it looks up the owning class via `obj.__globals__[cls_path]`, but for a decorated method (functools.wraps wrapper defined in another module) __globals__ is the WRAPPER's module globals, so the class is missing and napoleon_include_init_with_doc silently fails. Fix (matches upstream): `sphinx.util.inspect.unwrap(obj).__globals__[cls_path]` — use sphinx.util.inspect.unwrap, not stdlib inspect.unwrap, because it catches ValueError from mock objects. Repro needs the decorator in a DIFFERENT module than the class, else the class is in the wrapper's globals anyway. _skip_member is testable without a Sphinx app (SimpleNamespace with the three napoleon_include_* config attrs); tests/test_ext_napoleon.py needs no sphinxcontrib stubs. Also zsh gotcha: `status` is a read-only variable in zsh (alias for $?) — `status=$?` aborts the rest of a command list, silently skipping e.g. a trailing `git stash pop`.

content: Sphinx napoleon bug #8056 ("x1, x2 : array_like" multi-name numpy param renders garbled, "optional" lost): napoleon's reST output `:param x1, x2:` + `:type x1, x2:` looks fine — the actual breakage is in DocFieldTransformer.transform (sphinx/util/docfields.py), whose `:param type name:` syntax support does `fieldarg.split(None, 1)` and misparses "x1, x2" as type="x1," name="x2", so the bogus type wins and the real `:type` entry (keyed "x1, x2") is never matched. Upstream fix is napoleon-side, not docfields: GoogleDocstring._parse_parameters_section calls _consume_fields(multiple=True), and _consume_fields with multiple=True splits _name on commas into separate (name, type, desc) entries — one :param/:type pair per name, description duplicated. Only applies when napoleon_use_param=True; use_param=False must keep the combined "**x1, x2** (type)" via _format_fields. Quick e2e verify: tiny autodoc+napoleon project built with PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sphinx_type_hint_links/stubs python -m sphinx -b text.

content: Sphinx quickstart gotcha (bug #9367, sphinx/cmd/quickstart.py): do_prompt substitutes the default only via `if default and not x:` — so an EMPTY default ('') is never substituted and empty input goes straight to the validator. Any "press Enter to exit/skip" prompt therefore needs a validator that explicitly accepts '' (upstream fix: is_path_or_empty wrapping is_path); the `if not d['path']: sys.exit(1)` after the prompt is unreachable otherwise. Verify without a Sphinx app by monkeypatching quickstart.term_input and calling ask_user({'path': dir_with_conf_py}) expecting SystemExit. tests/test_quickstart.py needs the PYTHONPATH stubs only for test_quickstart_and_build.

content: Sphinx pycode ast gotcha (bug #9391, sphinx/pycode/ast.py): _UnparseVisitor.visit_Tuple rendered 1-element tuples without the trailing comma — "(1,)" became "(1)". Fix: special-case len(node.elts) == 1 → "(%s,)" % self.visit(node.elts[0]) (keep "()" for empty). Tuple rendering has TWO paths: visit_Subscript's is_simple_tuple deliberately joins without a trailing comma (Tuple[(int,)] → Tuple[int]) — leave that path alone. Pre-existing limitation in this 3.0.x-era checkout: there is no visit_Starred, so a top-level tuple containing *a raises NotImplementedError (Starred is only screened out inside subscript tuples). tests/test_pycode_ast.py needs no app fixture or env stubs; quick repro: sphinx.pycode.ast.unparse(ast.parse(src).body[0].value) — unparse takes an expression node, not a Module.

Sphinx autodoc mock bug #9658 ("Bases: torch.nn." instead of "torch.nn.Module" for classes inheriting mocked classes): mocked attributes are _MockObject INSTANCES (_MockModule.__getattr__ returns `_make_subclass(name, module)()` — note the call). Subclassing such an instance triggers PEP 560 __mro_entries__ (returns self.__class__), so Python records the mock INSTANCE in the subclass's __orig_bases__; ClassDocumenter.add_directive_header prefers __orig_bases__ over __bases__, and restify renders via `cls.__module__` + `cls.__qualname__` — but _MockObject.__init__ hardcoded `self.__qualname__ = ''`, producing "module." with the trailing dot and nothing after. Fix (matches upstream): in sphinx/ext/autodoc/mock.py add class attr `__name__ = ''` on _MockObject, add `'__name__': name` to _make_subclass attrs, and change __init__ to `self.__qualname__ = self.__name__`. Python subtlety: a '__name__' key in a class's creation dict is visible to instances via MRO dict lookup (classes themselves still get tp_name via type's data descriptor, same value), and type() already puts '__qualname__' in the class __dict__ — the instance attribute set in __init__ was shadowing it.
